chapters.title: Chapter 1610: Returning to Black Dragon Clan!
paragraphs: Max only gave a wry smile.
Truthfully, even he had not expected such an outcome.

After devouring the corpse of the ancient black dragon, he had assumed nearly all of the absorbed essence would be used to refine his bloodline and push the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline to its highest stage.

Instead, after the bloodline completed its transformation, the remaining power had surged through his body and raised his cultivation from the fifth level of the Law Awakening Realm straight to the eighth.
Even now, when he thought about it, the gains were absurd.
Lucia watched his expression and narrowed her eyes slightly.
There was something suspicious about the whole matter.

She knew Max had gone into Dragon Death Valley and returned stronger, but the extent of that growth was too unreasonable. Three levels at his stage, along with the deepened aura he now carried, clearly meant he had gained far more than he admitted.
Still, she did not press him.
Everyone had secrets, and Max had more than most.
Instead, she simply gave him a meaningful look.
"You really are impossible to measure."
Max laughed softly.
"I will take that as praise."
"You should."
Then, after a short pause, Max asked the question that mattered next.
"So when are we heading to Violet Star Palace for this Smelting Trial?"
Lucia answered without hesitation.
"In one week."
She leaned back in her seat and crossed her arms.

"The clan will need time to gather the selected participants, prepare supplies, and arrange the route. Violet Star Palace is not some nearby branch force. Even with star travel, reaching their territory requires proper planning."
Max nodded calmly.
"One week..."
That was enough time to consolidate his recent gains, become familiar with his new bloodline abilities, and perhaps make a few more preparations before entering another major opportunity.
Lucia glanced at him and smirked.
"Do not tell me you are already planning how to cause trouble there."
Max looked out toward the stars through the shuttle window and smiled faintly.
"I am planning how to become stronger."
Lucia sighed.
"That answer somehow worries me even more."
A few hours later, after traveling through countless streams of starlight and crossing several spatial routes, the star shuttle finally entered the territory of the Verdant Sky Realm.
The moment they crossed into its borders, the atmosphere outside the vessel subtly changed.
The stars here seemed brighter, and the surrounding spiritual currents were far richer than those near Orion.

Vast celestial islands floated in the distance, connected by rivers of light that drifted through space like living streams. Ancient mountain chains hung suspended above cloud oceans, while enormous beasts could occasionally be seen gliding between realms as naturally as birds crossing the sky.
Even the air carried a sense of old prosperity.
This was not a chaotic battlefield world like Orion.
This was a true realm shaped and ruled by powerful forces over countless years.
Lucia looked outside with a familiar calm, while Max observed everything with quiet interest.
"The Verdant Sky Realm..." he muttered.
Compared to many places he had seen recently, this realm possessed both order and strength.
The shuttle continued descending through layers of cloud and defensive formations. Brilliant runes lit up across the hull as it passed several checkpoints before being recognized and allowed through.
A few minutes later, the vessel lowered toward a secluded region hidden among enormous black mountains.
The area was isolated from the bustling zones of the realm, surrounded by towering peaks that curved inward like natural walls.

Thick forests covered the lower slopes, and dark mist drifted between the cliffs. Streams rich with energy flowed through the valleys, while ancient formations shimmered faintly across the land, concealing the region from ordinary eyes.
Then Max saw it.
The Black Dragon Palace.
It rested deep within the mountain basin like a silent sovereign fortress.

Its structures were built from dark stone and black metal, rising in grand layered halls and towering spires shaped with draconic motifs. Massive statues of black dragons coiled around pillars, while banners bearing the clan insignia moved in the wind. The palace did not flaunt luxury like some divine sects.
Instead, it radiated strength, discipline, and ancient pride.
The star shuttle descended slowly before landing on a wide stone platform near the outer palace grounds.
A deep mechanical hum faded as the vessel settled.
The hatch opened.

Max stepped out first and felt the familiar dense energy of the area brush against his skin immediately. It was many times richer than ordinary places and perfectly suited for cultivation unlike the chaotic aura of Orion.
He looked around the secluded basin and found there to be empty.
Lucia stepped out beside him and stretched lightly.
"We are home."
Max glanced toward the Black Dragon Palace once more.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"And just in time."
One week remained before the Smelting Trial.
"I think you should go and check on Aunt Virelia before going anywhere else," Lucia said as they stood near the landing platform. "She must have been worried about you this whole time."
Max nodded.

That had already been his intention. No matter how many opportunities he encountered outside, returning and meeting his master first was only natural. Lady Virelia had supported him from the beginning, and after everything that had happened on Orion, she would certainly want answers.
Just as Max was about to leave, Lucia suddenly spoke again.
"Wait."
He turned back.
Lucia crossed her arms and looked at him directly.
"You should release Isabella first."
Max blinked once, then immediately understood what she meant.
Lucia continued in a practical tone.

"She is one of the stronger young geniuses of our side and will likely be among those heading to Violet Star Palace for the Smelting Trial. We only have seven days left. If she remains hidden away any longer, she will lose valuable preparation time."
Her eyes narrowed slightly.
"And if she finds out you kept her inside your secret world while everyone else was preparing, she may personally try to kill you."
Max coughed lightly.
"That is also possible."
He could not deny her logic.
The Smelting Trial would gather elites from powerful factions. Even for someone talented like Isabella, entering such an event unprepared would be foolish.

chapters.title: Chapter 1611: Meeting Master!
paragraphs: "Fine," Max said with a nod.
With a thought, he opened a connection to the Dimension of Genesis.

Space rippled beside them, and Isabella stepped out from the hidden world into the open mountain basin of the Black Dragon Palace. She looked around briefly, taking in the familiar surroundings before her gaze landed on Max.
"So we are back."
Max smiled faintly.
"We are. And you should prepare well."
His tone became more serious.
"The Smelting Trial at Violet Star Palace begins soon. Use these seven days wisely. Strengthen yourself as much as possible."
Isabella’s eyes brightened immediately.
She had naturally heard of the Smelting Trial before. For disciples of third-rate forces, receiving the chance to participate in such an event was both opportunity and recognition.
"I am also heading there?" she asked.
Lucia answered before Max could.
"You were always likely to be selected as you are the Saintess of the Black Dragon Clan. Now stop wasting time and start preparing."
Isabella snorted softly but did not argue.
Then she looked back at Max, a faint smile appearing.
"You had better not grow too far ahead again in just seven days."
Max chuckled.
"I was about to say the same to you."
She rolled her eyes, though amusement remained clear on her face.
With that, Max left the two women together near the platform while they began discussing clan matters, trial participants, and possible preparations.
He then turned toward the deeper regions of the Black Dragon Palace and began walking alone.
Towering halls rose ahead of him, ancient and solemn beneath the mountain sky.
Soon Max arrived before the office of Lady Virelia.

The familiar corridor leading to her chambers carried the same quiet authority as before. Black stone walls lined with ancient carvings reflected the heritage of the Black Dragon Clan, while subtle defensive formations pulsed beneath the floor.
Even after everything he had experienced recently, returning here brought a strange sense of steadiness.
He raised his hand and knocked.
"Come in."
Without hesitation, Max opened the door and stepped inside.

Lady Virelia was seated comfortably on a long couch near a low table where tea had already been prepared. Sunlight from the side windows fell across the room, giving the otherwise stern office a warmer atmosphere.
Max walked forward and sat on the couch opposite her.
Lady Virelia looked at him for several moments before narrowing her eyes slightly.

"It seems Orion treated you rather generously," she said. "You left at the fifth level of the Law Awakening Realm and returned at the eighth. That is not the kind of progress one makes from sightseeing."
Max smiled wryly.
"Some things happened."

He then began recounting part of what had occurred on Orion. He spoke of the secret domain, the chaos among the gathered forces, the dangers of the forbidden regions, and the events that led to the conflict with Sword God Palace. However, he carefully omitted matters that should remain hidden, including the deeper truths of his personal gains.
Lady Virelia listened in silence while calmly sipping tea.
When he finished, she set the cup down gently.
"I already heard much of what happened," she said. "The news from Orion has spread throughout this side of the Divine Realm."
Her gaze sharpened.

"Those who escaped the secret domain returned shaken. Most of them still cannot explain what truly happened inside. They only know they were facing suppression from a terrifying existence one moment, and the next they were suddenly back on Orion."
Max nodded.
"That is more or less what it felt like."
He leaned back slightly.
"One moment we believed we might die, and the next we were alive again. Whatever the truth behind it is, I am not complaining."
Lady Virelia gave him a brief look that suggested she suspected he knew more than he admitted, but she did not press the matter.
Instead, she asked another question.
"I also heard that the four Primarchs of the Primordial Race appeared."
Max nodded.
"They did. Even from a distance, their presence was overwhelming."
Lady Virelia’s expression became solemn.
"Beings of that level rarely move without reason. If they appeared personally, then something inside that domain was significant."
She then changed topics.
"And then there is your matter with Sword God Palace."
Max remained calm.
Lady Virelia’s lips curved faintly.
"You truly know how to cause trouble. Offending Sword God Palace is not something ordinary disciples manage to accomplish in a lifetime, yet you did it in a single trip."
Max coughed lightly.
"They started it. They wanted my sword and they were so shameless about it that they wanted to kill me to take my sword away."
"Even so you did beat up the Young Miss of the Sword God Palace."
Even so, amusement flickered in her eyes.
She continued.
"I also heard about your interaction with War God Palace."
Her gaze became more meaningful now.

"Forming even a temporary alliance with 1st rate forces like War God Palace with them has raised your standing considerably. Many forces now view you, and by extension the Black Dragon Clan, differently."
Max nodded slowly.
"I understand."
Lady Virelia folded her hands before her.
"Good. Then understand this as well."
Her voice grew firmer.
"In seven days, the delegation heading to Violet Star Palace for the Smelting Trial will depart. You are no longer just another promising disciple."
She looked directly into his eyes.
"You will be one of the main faces of the Black Dragon Clan there."
Max straightened slightly.
She continued.

"Your name has already spread. Some know you as the one connected to the Sword Sovereign’s weapon. Some know of your conflict with Sword God Palace. Others know that War God Palace openly treated you with respect."
Her tone sharpened.
"That fame is useful, but it is also dangerous."
Max listened quietly.

"At the Smelting Trial, geniuses from many third-rate forces will be present. Some will want to test you. Some will want to humiliate you. Some may target you simply to weaken the Black Dragon Clan’s momentum."
She leaned forward slightly.
"So use these seven days well. Consolidate your cultivation. Prepare your methods. Do not grow complacent because of what happened on Orion."
Max smiled faintly.
"I never planned to be complacent."
Lady Virelia studied him for a moment, then gave a satisfied nod.
"Good."
She lifted her tea once more.
"Because whether you like it or not, many eyes are now waiting to see if you are truly worthy of the noise surrounding your name."

chapters.title: Chapter 1612: Vein of Strength
paragraphs: "Anyway, here are a few resources," Lady Virelia said as she took out a storage ring and placed it on the table before sliding it toward Max.
"It should be enough to raise your cultivation several times if used properly."
Max picked up the ring and sent a trace of his senses inside.

Even with only a brief glance, he could tell the contents were generous. Divine crystals, spirit medicines, condensed energy stones, and several rare materials were neatly arranged within. Any ordinary disciple would consider such wealth a fortune.
Lady Virelia continued calmly.
"I do not fully understand how your Seven Divine Veins function, but I also placed body-refining treasures inside. Some of them should help you attempt the opening of the third vein."
Max’s eyes brightened slightly.
"Oh."
He looked genuinely pleased.
"I really needed this."
He clenched the storage ring lightly.
"Recently my body has become far stronger than before. I can feel it clearly. If I have enough resources, opening another one or even two of the Seven Divine Veins should not be impossible."
Lady Virelia raised a brow.
"You say such outrageous things too casually."
Max laughed.
"I only speak according to what I feel."

She shook her head, though there was clear satisfaction in her expression. Max’s monstrous progress had long surpassed normal standards, and by now she had stopped trying to compare him with ordinary geniuses.
Then her tone became serious once more.
"With that said, use the remaining seven days entirely for training."
She tapped the table lightly.
"Do not waste time wandering around, provoking people, or chasing random opportunities."
Max coughed softly.
"I was not planning to."
Lady Virelia gave him a long look that made it clear she did not fully believe him.
"If you need assistance, techniques, resources, or access to restricted training grounds, come to me at any time during these seven days."
Her voice softened slightly.
"You are carrying much of the clan’s hopes into this Smelting Trial. I will support you where I can."
Max’s expression turned more sincere.
"I understand."
He gave a firm nod.
Lady Virelia leaned back into her seat.
"Good. Then leave and begin immediately."
Max stood up at once.
He bowed respectfully toward her.
"Thank you, Master."
A faint smile appeared on her face.
"Go."
Without saying anything further, Max turned and left the office.
The corridor outside was quiet, the palace halls still carrying their solemn atmosphere. As he walked through them, the storage ring in his hand felt heavier than its physical weight.
Not because of the treasures inside.
But because of the expectations placed upon him.
Soon, he exited the central palace grounds and headed toward his own residence within the Black Dragon Clan territory.
The path ahead was clear.
Seven days.
Seven days to grow stronger, open new veins, stabilize his gains from Orion, and prepare for the Smelting Trial at Violet Star Palace.
As he looked toward the distant silhouette of his house, a faint smile rose on his lips.
"That should be enough time."
Arriving back at his house, Max wasted no time. He went straight into the training chamber, sealed the room, activated the protective formations, and then entered the Dimension of Time.
The endless white world unfolded around him in silence.

Max sat cross-legged in the middle of that vast emptiness and took out all the body cultivation resources Lady Virelia had given him. One by one, he placed them before himself. There were blood-red crystals filled with violent vitality, bottles of thick golden marrow liquid, dark stones that released heavy physical pressure, and several strange herbs whose roots pulsed like living veins.
All of them were treasures meant to strengthen the body.

For ordinary cultivators, using even one of these resources recklessly could damage the meridians, tear muscles apart, or overload the bones. But Max was different now. After devouring the corpse of the ancient black dragon, his physique had changed completely.

His body contained 5000 Draconic Essences, each one like a miniature furnace of raw draconic power. His 5000 Dragon Scales had also strengthened his flesh, bones, blood, and organs to an astonishing level.
Because of that, his body was no longer fragile in front of violent energy.
It was like a divine weapon waiting to be further tempered.
Max closed his eyes and activated the method of the Seven Divine Veins.

The first two Divine Veins within his body responded immediately. They pulsed with deep power, guiding the flow of energy through him. After a few breaths, Max focused his senses on the hidden location of the third Divine Vein.
The Vein of Strength.

Unlike ordinary veins or meridians, the Divine Veins were not simple channels of energy. They were ancient gates hidden within the body, each representing a different form of physical power. The Vein of Strength was buried deep within his flesh and bones, connected to every muscle fiber, every tendon, and every part of his physical foundation.
To open it, Max did not need delicate comprehension.
He needed overwhelming bodily force.
He needed to awaken the raw power sleeping inside his body and force it to recognize him as its master.
Max picked up the first blood-red crystal and crushed it in his palm.

A thick wave of vitality surged out and entered his body like molten blood. At the same time, he drank the golden marrow liquid and swallowed several body-refining herbs. The combined power of these resources exploded inside him almost instantly.
Boom!
His body trembled.

For a normal cultivator, that violent eruption would have been dangerous. It would have torn through the body like a storm. But the moment the energy spread, the 5000 Draconic Essences inside Max awakened together.
They absorbed, refined, and controlled the incoming force.

The chaotic vitality was dragged into his bones. The marrow liquid seeped into his spine and limbs. The medicinal power of the herbs entered his muscles and tendons. Instead of harming him, all of it became fuel.
Max’s skin began glowing faintly.

Underneath his flesh, black dragon patterns appeared one after another, moving like living marks across his body. His blood flowed faster, each beat of his heart echoing like a war drum inside the silent white world.
He guided all the power toward the third Divine Vein.
At first, the Vein of Strength remained still.
It was like a sealed mountain gate, heavy and ancient, refusing to open no matter how much energy struck it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1613 - 9th level of Law Awakening Realm!
paragraphs: Max was not surprised.
He took out more resources and consumed them without hesitation.

This time, the pressure in his body increased severalfold. His muscles expanded slightly, then compressed again. His bones released crisp cracking sounds as they were washed by the gathered power. Every inch of his flesh felt as though it was being hammered by invisible divine blacksmiths.
But Max did not show pain.
Compared to the torment he had endured in the past, this was nothing.
More importantly, his body was too strong now.

The 5000 Dragon Scales formed a hidden protective layer beneath his skin, preventing the violent energy from damaging his physical structure. The 5000 Draconic Essences acted like anchors, stabilizing every surge of power and forcing it to move according to his will.
Because of this, the process that should have been extremely dangerous became almost smooth.
Max continued gathering force.
One wave.
Two waves.
Ten waves.
All of the energy slammed into the sealed Vein of Strength again and again.
Gradually, the hidden Divine Vein began to react.
A deep rumbling sound echoed inside his body.
Max’s eyes snapped open for a brief moment.
"Found it."

He immediately activated Dragon Scales Transformation, but only partially. Thin black scales appeared across his arms, chest, and shoulders, strengthening his body even further. At the same time, his draconic aura surged, causing the endless white space around him to tremble slightly.
Then Max clenched both fists and roared inwardly.
"Open."
The gathered energy transformed into a violent current and rushed toward the third Divine Vein.
Bang!
The first impact shook his entire body.
Bang!
The second impact caused cracks to appear across the invisible barrier sealing the vein.
Bang!
The third impact made the Vein of Strength shine with a deep crimson-gold light.
Max did not stop.

He burned through more body cultivation resources and pushed every strand of energy toward that single point. His heart pounded harder. His blood boiled. His muscles trembled not from weakness, but from the rising force waiting to erupt.
Then, finally, the seal shattered.
BOOM!
A terrifying wave of strength exploded from within Max’s body.
The third Divine Vein opened.
The Vein of Strength awakened.
In an instant, Max felt as if a new source of power had been born inside him. It spread through his body with brutal simplicity, strengthening his arms, legs, back, chest, bones, tendons, and organs.
It did not feel like energy being added from the outside. It felt as though his body had remembered a power it was always meant to possess.
His muscles became denser.
His bones became heavier and stronger.
His flesh gained a terrifying explosive force.
Every movement of his body now carried a deeper physical dominance than before.

The 5000 Draconic Essences also reacted to the opening of the Vein of Strength. They pulsed together, synchronizing with the new Divine Vein. His Dragon Scales grew even tougher, and the physical strength contained within each scale increased.
Max slowly stood up.
The moment he rose, the ground of the Dimension of Time trembled beneath his feet.
He looked down at his hands and clenched them lightly.
Crack.
The air around his fist distorted from the pressure alone.
A smile appeared on his face.
"The third Divine Vein..."
He could feel it clearly.

The Vein of Strength had not simply increased his raw power. It had multiplied the efficiency of his entire body. Every punch, every kick, every sword swing, and every movement would now carry far greater force than before.

With his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline complete, 5000 Draconic Essences, 5000 Dragon Scales, and now the Vein of Strength opened, his physical body had reached a level that even many higher-realm geniuses would find terrifying.
Max took a slow breath and allowed the remaining medicinal power to settle.
The process had gone smoother than he expected.

If he had attempted this before devouring the black dragon corpse, opening the third Divine Vein would have been difficult and dangerous. But now, with his transformed physique, the barrier that once seemed challenging had become something he could break through with steady force.
He looked at the remaining resources before him.
"There is still some left."
His eyes gleamed faintly.
"Then I should not waste it."
Max looked at the remaining resources spread before him and did not waste a single moment.
The opening of the third Divine Vein had consumed a large portion of the body cultivation treasures, yet Lady Virelia’s preparations had been generous.

Several bottles of condensed divine essence still remained, along with spirit stones rich in law energy, two rare fruits wrapped in natural runes, and a cluster of pale crystals that released pure cultivation force.
For many disciples, this leftover amount alone would have been enough to support months of training.
For Max, it was another step forward.

He sat down once more in the endless white world of the Dimension of Time and calmed his breathing. The newly opened Vein of Strength pulsed steadily within him, while the first two Divine Veins resonated in harmony. His body now felt heavier, denser, and vastly more powerful than before.
Then he began cultivating.
Max crushed the pale crystals first.

They dissolved into streams of radiant energy that entered his pores and flowed directly into his meridians. He followed by swallowing the two spirit fruits, whose rich essence spread through his organs like warm currents of liquid light. Finally, he opened the bottles of divine essence and drank them one after another.
At once, a tremendous amount of energy gathered inside him.
Ordinary cultivators would have needed to stop and carefully refine each layer of power, but Max’s body was no longer ordinary.
The complete Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline refined energy with frightening efficiency.
The 5000 Draconic Essences absorbed impurities and converted raw force into nourishment.
The 5000 Dragon Scales stabilized his physique.
The three opened Divine Veins pulled in energy like hungry stars.
Even so, Max’s body required an absurd amount of resources.
What would fill a lake for others only became a river for him.
He activated his cultivation art and drew every strand of power inward. Waves of energy circled around him again and again, compressed, refined, and pushed toward the barrier of the next level.
Hours passed within the Dimension of Time.
The pressure inside his dantian rose steadily.
The aura around him thickened.
Then, with a deep rumble, the final layer of resistance gave way.
Boom.
A surge of force erupted from Max’s body and swept across the white world like a shockwave.
His cultivation advanced.
Ninth level of the Law Awakening Realm.
Max slowly opened his eyes. They shone with deeper power than before.
He exhaled and let the remaining traces of energy settle.
"If this were another cultivator..." he murmured.
He knew the truth clearly.
With the same quantity of resources, many geniuses would have broken through two or even three levels. Some ordinary cultivators might have advanced even more.
But Max’s foundation was too monstrous.
Every realm of his required vast oceans of energy because each breakthrough strengthened not only cultivation, but also bloodline, body, Divine Veins, and countless hidden foundations.
What others gained in speed, he gained in depth.
And Max was fully satisfied with that.
A weak foundation that rose quickly meant little.
A terrifying foundation that rose steadily could shake worlds.
He stood up and clenched his fist lightly.
The aura of the ninth level of Law Awakening Realm flowed naturally through him, perfectly stable and without the slightest sign of instability.
Combined with the Vein of Strength and his completed bloodline, his combat power had risen far beyond what a simple level increase suggested.
Max smiled faintly.
"One more step closer."
And he was far from finished preparing.

His Dragon Scales grew even tougher, and the physical strength contained within each scale increased.
Max slowly stood up.
The moment he rose, the ground of the Dimension of Time trembled beneath his feet.
He looked down at his hands and clenched them lightly.
Crack.
The air around his fist distorted from the pressure alone.
A smile appeared on his face.
"The third Divine Vein..."
He could feel it clearly.
The Vein of Strength had not simply increased his raw power.
It had multiplied the efficiency of his entire body.
Every punch, every kick, every sword swing, and every movement would now carry far greater force than before.

With his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline complete, 5000 Draconic Essences, 5000 Dragon Scales, and now the Vein of Strength opened, his physical body had reached a level that even many higher-realm geniuses would find terrifying.
Max took a slow breath and allowed the remaining medicinal power to settle.
The process had gone smoother than he expected.
If he had attempted this before devouring the black dragon corpse, opening the third Divine Vein would have been difficult and dangerous.
But now, with his transformed physique, the barrier that once seemed challenging had become something he could break through with steady force.
He looked at the remaining resources before him.
"There is still some left."
His eyes gleamed faintly.
"Then I should not waste it."
Max looked at the remaining resources spread before him and did not waste a single moment.
The opening of the third Divine Vein had consumed a large portion of the body cultivation treasures, yet Lady Virelia’s preparations had been generous.

Several bottles of condensed divine essence still remained, along with spirit stones rich in law energy, two rare fruits wrapped in natural runes, and a cluster of pale crystals that released pure cultivation force.
For many disciples, this leftover amount alone would have been enough to support months of training.
For Max, it was another step forward.
He sat down once more in the endless white world of the Dimension of Time and calmed his breathing.
The newly opened Vein of Strength pulsed steadily within him, while the first two Divine Veins resonated in harmony.
His body now felt heavier, denser, and vastly more powerful than before.
Then he began cultivating.
Max crushed the pale crystals first.
They dissolved into streams of radiant energy that entered his pores and flowed directly into his meridians.
He followed by swallowing the two spirit fruits, whose rich essence spread through his organs like warm currents of liquid light.
Finally, he opened the bottles of divine essence and drank them one after another.
At once, a tremendous amount of energy gathered inside him.
Ordinary cultivators would have needed to stop and carefully refine each layer of power, but Max’s body was no longer ordinary.
The complete Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline refined energy with frightening efficiency.
The 5000 Draconic Essences absorbed impurities and converted raw force into nourishment.
The 5000 Dragon Scales stabilized his physique.
The three opened Divine Veins pulled in energy like hungry stars.
Even so, Max’s body required an absurd amount of resources.
What would fill a lake for others only became a river for him.
He activated his cultivation art and drew every strand of power inward.
Waves of energy circled around him again and again, compressed, refined, and pushed toward the barrier of the next level.
Hours passed within the Dimension of Time.
The pressure inside his dantian rose steadily.
The aura around him thickened.
Then, with a deep rumble, the final layer of resistance gave way.
Boom.
A surge of force erupted from Max’s body and swept across the white world like a shockwave.
His cultivation advanced.
Ninth level of the Law Awakening Realm.
Max slowly opened his eyes.
They shone with deeper power than before.
He exhaled and let the remaining traces of energy settle.
"If this were another cultivator..." he murmured.
He knew the truth clearly.
With the same quantity of resources, many geniuses would have broken through two or even three levels.
Some ordinary cultivators might have advanced even more.
But Max’s foundation was too monstrous.
Every realm of his required vast oceans of energy because each breakthrough strengthened not only cultivation, but also bloodline, body, Divine Veins, and countless hidden foundations.
What others gained in speed, he gained in depth.
And Max was fully satisfied with that.
A weak foundation that rose quickly meant little.
A terrifying foundation that rose steadily could shake worlds.
He stood up and clenched his fist lightly.
The aura of the ninth level of Law Awakening Realm flowed naturally through him, perfectly stable and without the slightest sign of instability.
Combined with the Vein of Strength and his completed bloodline, his combat power had risen far beyond what a simple level increase suggested.
Max smiled faintly.
"One more step closer."
And he was far from finished preparing.

chapters.title: Chapter 1614: Gathering of True Disciples!
paragraphs: After reaching the ninth level of the Law Awakening Realm, Max carefully examined his condition and quickly came to a clear conclusion.
For the moment, he had reached the limit of what he could improve through direct cultivation.

He had already opened the third Divine Vein of the Seven Divine Veins, the Vein of Strength. Every remaining resource given by Lady Virelia had also been fully consumed to support his breakthrough into the ninth level of the Law Awakening Realm.
His internal growth had not stopped forever, but it had paused until he obtained new opportunities.
"My body is still strong enough to open the fourth Divine Vein," Max muttered to himself. "The Vein of Speed should be within reach."
He clenched and relaxed his hand slowly, sensing the terrifying vitality in his flesh.
"But I do not have enough resources."
Opening a Divine Vein required more than toughness. It demanded vast treasures, body-refining materials, and enough energy to force open another ancient gate hidden within the physique.
Max was not discouraged.
Instead, his eyes sharpened with anticipation.
"The Smelting Trial should provide what I need."

He believed that an event jointly organized by powerful forces would contain inheritances, treasures, and rare resources beyond what ordinary cultivators could imagine. If fortune favored him there, opening the fourth Divine Vein and reaching the tenth level of Law Awakening Realm before the Cosmic Ascension Conference was entirely possible.
That thought alone was enough motivation.
"Then I should use the remaining time to sharpen what I already have."
With that, Max rose from where he sat in the endless white world of the Dimension of Time.
"Let us see whether the inheritance chambers have anything new for me."
He stepped forward and entered the Dimension of Flames for a new inheritance technique.

After leaving the Dimension of Flames, Max did not remain idle for even a moment. He continued moving through one dimension after another, entering the Dimension of Sword, the Dimension of Ice, the Dimension of Light, the Dimension of Lightning, the Dimension of Space, and several other worlds connected to his growing dimensional inheritance.
Each world possessed its own inheritance chamber, and within each chamber were techniques preserved from powerful beings of the past.

Once his choices were complete, Max returned to the Dimension of Time. The endless white world welcomed him with its usual silence, a place where one hour outside equaled one full year within. The moment he arrived, he began training without hesitation.
Days passed first, then months, and eventually years. Outside, only seven short days moved by. Inside, decades of relentless cultivation unfolded.

Max trained sword techniques until every slash, thrust, and counterattack became second nature. He practiced movement arts until he could transition from lightning speed to light acceleration and then into spatial displacement without even needing conscious thought.
He refined close combat methods until every punch and kick carried monstrous force through the awakened Vein of Strength.

He repeated elemental techniques countless times. He fused methods together, tore apart flaws, and reshaped inheritances into forms more suitable for himself. Fire techniques gained sharper killing intent.

Lightning arts became more efficient. Spatial methods became harder to predict. Whenever one cycle of training ended, another began immediately. There was no laziness, no wasted time, and no room for complacency.

By the time the seven days in the outside world had passed, decades had flowed for Max within the Dimension of Time. His cultivation realm remained at the ninth level of the Law Awakening Realm, yet his true strength had increased dramatically.

His aura became deeper and more restrained, his instincts sharper, and his movements smoother. He now carried the calm pressure of someone who had tempered himself through long years of isolation and battle practice.
At last, Max slowly opened his eyes and exhaled a steady breath. He could clearly feel the connection between the outer world and the Dimension of Time shifting.
"Seven days have passed," he muttered softly.
With that, he left the Dimension of Time and returned to his house.
The familiar training chamber greeted him once more. Max quickly washed away the dust of long training, took a proper bath, and changed into clean robes.
Afterward, he sat down and ate a meal in peace. Even something as ordinary as food felt refreshing after spending decades focused only on cultivation and combat.
Just then, a powerful voice echoed throughout the entirety of the Black Dragon Palace. It rolled through halls, courtyards, mountains, and training grounds like thunder striking the heavens.
"All True Disciples, report at the Central Region of the Black Dragon Palace."
Max looked up calmly as the announcement repeated across the clan territory. He set down the last of his meal, stood from his seat, and adjusted his robes.
"It is time," he said quietly.
He then stepped out of his house and headed toward the Central Region of the Black Dragon Palace.
When Max arrived at the Central Region of the Black Dragon Palace, the place was already bustling with activity.

The Central Region was one of the grandest areas within the clan territory, built upon a vast elevated platform surrounded by towering halls, training arenas, and black stone pillars carved with dragon patterns. Ancient banners fluttered in the wind, and layered formations shimmered faintly beneath the ground, revealing the importance of the place.
At the center of the platform, a group of true disciples had already gathered.
Max’s gaze swept over them once and immediately sharpened.
There were a little over thirty of them in total.

Some stood calmly with arms folded. Others conversed in low voices with familiar allies. A few sat cross-legged in meditation despite the gathering, as though using every moment to cultivate. Their expressions varied, but one thing was common among them all.
They were strong.
Very strong.
The aura coming from this group far surpassed that of ordinary disciples. These were the elite geniuses of the Black Dragon Clan, the younger generation chosen to represent the clan in major events.
Max silently observed them more carefully.

Most of them possessed cultivation beyond the fifth level of the Law Manifestation Realm. Several had already reached the seventh and eighth levels, their presence stable and imposing. A smaller number stood out even more, carrying dense pressure that caused those nearby to unconsciously keep some distance.
Those few had already reached the ninth and tenth levels of the Law Manifestation Realm.

chapters.title: Chapter 1615: Wonders of Chaos Fruit!
paragraphs: Even Max’s eyes narrowed when he sensed them.
He had known the Black Dragon Clan would send its strongest talents, but seeing the group gathered together in one place still made the reality clearer.
These were not ordinary geniuses.

They were individuals who had grown within one of the Divine Realm’s weakest third rate force. Max could only imagine what sort of geniuses the 1st rate forces would have in the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
As Max looked at them, he recalled his earlier conversation with Lucia during their journey to Orion.
At that time, she had spoken of how nearly every genius in the Divine Realm sought to reach the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm before the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Now, standing here and seeing this scene, Max could not help but admit that her words had not been wrong.
Almost all true talents in the Divine Realm clearly aimed for that same benchmark.
And the Black Dragon Clan was no exception.
The disciples gathered before him were proof of it.

Many had likely spent years preparing for this period. They had tempered themselves, accumulated resources, and suppressed breakthroughs at key moments in order to arrive at the Smelting Trial in their strongest possible condition.
Max’s own cultivation at the ninth level of the Law Awakening Realm stood noticeably lower than nearly everyone present.
Yet he did not feel pressured.
Instead, his interest only deepened.
The stronger the competition, the greater the value of surpassing it.
Some disciples soon noticed his arrival.
A few eyes immediately changed when they recognized him. Others began whispering quietly among themselves. Several looked openly curious, while some gazes carried challenge or doubt.
After all, Max’s reputation had spread recently, but reputation and cultivation were two different matters.
Many had heard stories.
Now they were seeing the man himself.
Max ignored their reactions and simply walked forward with calm steps before taking a place among the gathered disciples.
His aura remained restrained, giving little away.
Yet beneath that calm exterior, his eyes were bright.
The Smelting Trial had not even begun, and already he could feel the pressure of true competition gathering around him.
"Max!"
Soon after he joined the gathered disciples, Lucia and Isabella made their way toward him through the crowd.
Both women stood out immediately.
Lucia carried her usual composed confidence, while Isabella’s presence seemed sharper and brighter than before, as though something fundamental within her had changed.
Max’s eyes first landed on Lucia.

With only a brief sense of her aura, he could tell that her strength had advanced again. She had already reached the sixth level of the Law Manifestation Realm. Her cultivation was steady, refined, and clearly consolidated after the progress made during the past week.
Then his attention shifted toward Isabella.
The moment he sensed her properly, Max’s expression changed.
"Huh?"
He stared at her for a moment.
"Isabella... your cultivation..."
There was genuine shock in his voice.
Her aura was no longer that of someone at the Law Awakening Realm.
She had already reached the fifth level of the Law Manifestation Realm.

Max remembered clearly that the last time he had checked, Isabella had only been at the second level of the Law Awakening Realm. Yet in the span of a single week, she had crossed the entirety of the Law Refinement Realm and broken through multiple smaller realms beyond that.
Such progress was outrageous even by genius standards.
Isabella folded her arms and lifted her chin proudly.
"Hehe, surprised?"
Max looked at her silently for another second.
"That is one way to put it."
Her smile widened.
"When I was training last week, my Imperial Bloodline fully awakened."
The pride in her voice was impossible to miss.

"The moment it awakened, my cultivation began breaking through repeatedly. The elders examined me afterward and said my strength should continue rising steadily until I eventually reach the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm."
Max blinked once.
Even for him, hearing that was absurd.
A bloodline awakening that could continue pushing cultivation forward over time was the kind of blessing countless people would dream about.
"Hehe, good for you," Max said with a smile that looked sincere enough on the surface.
Unfortunately for him, the faint trace of jealousy hidden in his eyes was far less convincing.
Lucia nearly laughed on the spot.
Isabella noticed it immediately and became even more pleased.
"Hehe, thank you, Max."
Her voice then sounded directly in his mind through divine transmission.
"Without the fruit you gave me, my Imperial Bloodline would not have awakened so soon."
Max’s expression shifted slightly.
She continued privately.
"That fruit was miraculous. It not only transformed my foundation and gave me a divine body, but it also stimulated the dormant Imperial Bloodline within me."
Her tone carried real gratitude now.
"Without it, I would likely have needed several more years before my bloodline fully awakened."
Max listened carefully.
The fruit she referred to was the Chaos Fruit he had once given her.
At the time, he had known it was precious and powerful, but even he had not expected it to trigger the awakening of a hidden bloodline.
"I see," Max replied inwardly.
He glanced at Isabella again, this time with deeper understanding.
So that was the reason behind her explosive growth.
The Chaos Fruit had refined her body, strengthened her foundation, and accelerated the awakening of her Imperial Bloodline all at once.
No wonder her cultivation had risen like a flood breaking through a dam.
Lucia looked between the two of them suspiciously.
"You two are being strangely quiet."
Max immediately smiled.
"We were just appreciating how talented Isabella has become."
Isabella nodded seriously.
"That is true."
Lucia narrowed her eyes, clearly unconvinced.
Still, she said nothing further.

Around them, several gathered disciples had also begun noticing Isabella’s transformed aura and discussing it in low voices. Others looked toward Max with renewed curiosity, wondering what kind of people were suddenly rising around him.
Max exhaled softly.
In only one week, both Lucia and Isabella had improved greatly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1616: Towards the Violet Star Palace!
paragraphs: Max looked around the gathering once more.
A little over thirty true disciples stood assembled across the vast platform, each one carrying a powerful aura and the confidence of someone selected from among the clan’s younger generation.
Yet considering the size and reputation of the Black Dragon Clan, the number still felt smaller than expected.
He turned toward Lucia.
"Is this all?"
Lucia raised a brow.
"All?"
Max gestured lightly toward the gathered crowd.
"I mean, is this the full number of true disciples in the Black Dragon Palace?"
Lucia immediately understood what he meant and smiled.
"No, of course not."
She folded her arms and glanced around the platform.
"These are only the true disciples eligible to attend the Smelting Trial."
Max’s eyes sharpened slightly.
"There is a requirement?"
"Naturally."
Her tone carried the faint amusement of someone explaining something obvious.

"The Smelting Trial is not a sightseeing trip. It is an event where talented disciples from many forces compete for opportunities, inheritances, and resources. Sending weaker disciples would only embarrass the clan and waste precious slots."
She then spoke more clearly.
"For this trip, only true disciples whose cultivation has reached the fifth level of the Law Manifestation Realm or higher were selected."
Max nodded inwardly.
That explained the strength of nearly everyone present.
Those below that threshold had likely been excluded no matter how talented they were. The clan clearly intended to send only those with enough power to compete immediately.
Then Lucia looked at him with a teasing smile.
"Of course..."
"You are an exception."
Max gave her a flat look.
"I had guessed that."
Lucia laughed softly.
"You should."
She stepped a little closer and lowered her voice.
"You are going because of your status as the Saint of the Black Dragon Clan."
Several nearby disciples subtly reacted when they heard the title.
Though many already knew, hearing it spoken aloud still carried weight.
Lucia continued.
"Your cultivation may still be at the Law Awakening Realm, but your position is different. You are no ordinary disciple being judged only by realm."
She glanced at him meaningfully.
"The elders also know very well that your real combat strength cannot be measured by cultivation level alone."
Max smiled faintly.
"So I was carried in through privilege."
Lucia snorted.
"If it were only privilege, many people here would object."
Her gaze swept across the platform.
"The reason no one openly complains is because they know you have already proven enough."
Max followed her gaze.
Several disciples were indeed looking toward him with mixed emotions. Some were curious. Some doubtful. Some openly competitive.
But none appeared dismissive enough to protest his presence.
Lucia then added one final remark.
"Still, being the exception means something else."
"What?"
"It means more people will watch you fail."
Max laughed softly.
"And if I succeed?"
Lucia’s smile deepened.
"Then they will hate you even more."
Isabella, who had been listening nearby, nodded seriously.
"That sounds accurate."
Max looked at the gathered elites of the Black Dragon Clan and then toward the distant palace towers beyond them.
Soon, powerful auras descended one after another over the Central Region.

The gathered true disciples immediately became serious as elders of the Black Dragon Clan appeared in the sky above the platform. Each elder stood calmly in midair, radiating strength and authority. Their arrival alone caused the atmosphere below to become tense and disciplined.
Then seven figures stepped forward at the front of the elders.
The moment they appeared, everyone recognized them instantly.
These were the heads of the Seven Main Families, the true ruling pillars of the Black Dragon Clan.
At the center stood Mathew Grimes, leader of the Grimes Family and the current highest authority overseeing the clan.
He stood with his hands behind his back, his presence steady and heavy like a mountain. His sharp eyes swept across the gathered disciples, causing the last whispers below to disappear.
When complete silence fell, he spoke.
"The Smelting Trial begins now."
His calm voice echoed across the entire region.
"You were chosen because you are the strongest of this generation. At Violet Star Palace, you will face geniuses from many forces. Some will underestimate you. Some will challenge you."
He paused briefly.
"Do not forget that when they look at you, they see the Black Dragon Clan."
Many disciples straightened unconsciously.
"Fight well. Win what you can. Protect the dignity of our clan."
His eyes sharpened.
"And if anyone thinks we are easy to bully..."
A faint pressure spread from him.
"Prove them wrong."
The blood of many disciples stirred instantly.
Then Mathew raised one hand toward the sky.
"Prepare to depart."
With his short speech finished, Mathew Grimes lifted one hand and waved it calmly through the air.
The space above the Central Region trembled.
A deep mechanical hum echoed across the platform as a massive star shuttle slowly emerged from a spatial fold high above them. Its appearance immediately drew every gaze upward.
The vessel was enormous.

Its body was forged from dark metallic material that shimmered with faint runic light. Layers of formations glowed across its surface like living constellations. Dragon patterns were carved along the outer hull, while black crystal wings extended from both sides, giving it the appearance of a celestial beast prepared to cross the void.
The pressure radiating from it made clear that this was no ordinary transport craft.
This was a true clan vessel built for long-distance star travel and protected against dangers of the cosmic void.
As it descended, powerful currents of wind swept across the platform. The shuttle then came to a stop above the ground, lowering a wide staircase of light toward the gathered disciples.
An elder stepped forward and announced firmly.
"All selected true disciples, board immediately."
At once, movement began.
The gathered disciples advanced in orderly lines, one after another entering the star shuttle. Though many were proud geniuses, no one acted recklessly in front of the family heads and elders.
Max watched calmly for a moment before stepping forward.
Lucia moved beside him with her usual composed expression, while Isabella walked on his other side, carrying herself with visible confidence after the awakening of her Imperial Bloodline.
The three of them approached the staircase together.

As Max stepped onto the light bridge, he glanced once at the enormous vessel above and could not help admiring the Black Dragon Clan’s foundation. Even a weaker third-rate force still possessed strength and wealth far beyond ordinary powers.
They soon entered the shuttle interior.

Inside, the space was far larger than what the exterior suggested. Wide halls, rows of seats, cultivation rooms, private chambers, and formation chambers had all been built within. The walls glowed with protective runes, and dense spiritual energy flowed through the vessel like hidden rivers.
As Max, Lucia, and Isabella moved inward, Max’s eyes shifted toward another entrance.
There, Lady Virelia was also stepping into the shuttle along with several elders.
Their eyes met briefly.
Lady Virelia gave him a calm nod that carried both approval and warning.
Max returned the gesture respectfully.
It was clear she would be accompanying the younger generation to Violet Star Palace.
One by one, the remaining disciples continued boarding until the final selected genius entered the vessel. Soon after, the staircase of light withdrew, and the outer gates sealed with a heavy sound.
Inside the shuttle, the atmosphere turned expectant.
Some disciples closed their eyes to meditate. Some whispered among friends. Others looked outward through crystal viewing panels, eager for what awaited them.
Then the formations of the star shuttle activated fully.
Runes across the vessel ignited with brilliant light.
A low vibration spread through the floors.
Outside, the giant craft slowly rose into the air above the Central Region of the Black Dragon Palace. Elders and clan members below looked upward as the vessel ascended higher and higher.
Then, with a sudden burst of celestial light, the star shuttle shot forward.
It tore through the sky like a black star, crossed the clouds in an instant, and vanished into the endless sea of stars.
The journey to Violet Star Palace had begun.

sentences.text: Max looked around the gathering once more.
A little over thirty true disciples stood assembled across the vast platform, each one carrying a powerful aura and the confidence of someone selected from among the clan’s younger generation.
Yet considering the size and reputation of the Black Dragon Clan, the number still felt smaller than expected.
He turned toward Lucia.
"Is this all?"
Lucia raised a brow.
"All?"
Max gestured lightly toward the gathered crowd.
"I mean, is this the full number of true disciples in the Black Dragon Palace?"
Lucia immediately understood what he meant and smiled.
"No, of course not."
She folded her arms and glanced around the platform.
"These are only the true disciples eligible to attend the Smelting Trial."
Max’s eyes sharpened slightly.
"There is a requirement?"
"Naturally."
Her tone carried the faint amusement of someone explaining something obvious.
"The Smelting Trial is not a sightseeing trip.
It is an event where talented disciples from many forces compete for opportunities, inheritances, and resources.
Sending weaker disciples would only embarrass the clan and waste precious slots."
She then spoke more clearly.
"For this trip, only true disciples whose cultivation has reached the fifth level of the Law Manifestation Realm or higher were selected."
Max nodded inwardly.
That explained the strength of nearly everyone present.
Those below that threshold had likely been excluded no matter how talented they were.
The clan clearly intended to send only those with enough power to compete immediately.
Then Lucia looked at him with a teasing smile.
"Of course..."
"You are an exception."
Max gave her a flat look.
"I had guessed that."
Lucia laughed softly.
"You should."
She stepped a little closer and lowered her voice.
"You are going because of your status as the Saint of the Black Dragon Clan."
Several nearby disciples subtly reacted when they heard the title.
Though many already knew, hearing it spoken aloud still carried weight.
Lucia continued.
"Your cultivation may still be at the Law Awakening Realm, but your position is different.
You are no ordinary disciple being judged only by realm."
She glanced at him meaningfully.
"The elders also know very well that your real combat strength cannot be measured by cultivation level alone."
Max smiled faintly.
"So I was carried in through privilege."
Lucia snorted.
"If it were only privilege, many people here would object."
Her gaze swept across the platform.
"The reason no one openly complains is because they know you have already proven enough."
Max followed her gaze.
Several disciples were indeed looking toward him with mixed emotions.
Some were curious.
Some doubtful.
Some openly competitive.
But none appeared dismissive enough to protest his presence.
Lucia then added one final remark.
"Still, being the exception means something else."
"What?"
"It means more people will watch you fail."
Max laughed softly.
"And if I succeed?"
Lucia’s smile deepened.
"Then they will hate you even more."
Isabella, who had been listening nearby, nodded seriously.
"That sounds accurate."
Max looked at the gathered elites of the Black Dragon Clan and then toward the distant palace towers beyond them.
Soon, powerful auras descended one after another over the Central Region.
The gathered true disciples immediately became serious as elders of the Black Dragon Clan appeared in the sky above the platform.
Each elder stood calmly in midair, radiating strength and authority.
Their arrival alone caused the atmosphere below to become tense and disciplined.
Then seven figures stepped forward at the front of the elders.
The moment they appeared, everyone recognized them instantly.
These were the heads of the Seven Main Families, the true ruling pillars of the Black Dragon Clan.
At the center stood Mathew Grimes, leader of the Grimes Family and the current highest authority overseeing the clan.
He stood with his hands behind his back, his presence steady and heavy like a mountain.
His sharp eyes swept across the gathered disciples, causing the last whispers below to disappear.
When complete silence fell, he spoke.
"The Smelting Trial begins now."
His calm voice echoed across the entire region.
"You were chosen because you are the strongest of this generation.
At Violet Star Palace, you will face geniuses from many forces.
Some will underestimate you.
Some will challenge you."
He paused briefly.
"Do not forget that when they look at you, they see the Black Dragon Clan."
Many disciples straightened unconsciously.
"Fight well.
Win what you can.
Protect the dignity of our clan."
His eyes sharpened.
"And if anyone thinks we are easy to bully..."
A faint pressure spread from him.
"Prove them wrong."

chapters.title: Chapter 1617: Arriving at the Violet Star Palace!
paragraphs: Hours passed as the star shuttle traveled through the cosmic void.

Protected by powerful runes and guided through stable star routes known only to major forces, the journey remained smooth. During that time, many disciples cultivated quietly, while others observed the passing wonders beyond the crystal viewing panels.
At last, the atmosphere inside the vessel shifted.
An elder announced that they had entered the territory of the Violet Star Realm.
Max stepped near one of the viewing panels and looked outside.
What he saw immediately drew his attention.
Before them stretched an enormous star realm filled with life and structure. Countless planets revolved through the vastness of space, each following precise celestial patterns.

Some worlds glowed with rich spiritual light. Others were wrapped in rings of mist or elemental storms. Massive floating fortresses drifted between planetary routes, while streams of star traffic moved in controlled lanes.
There were thousands of planets within the Violet Star Realm.
It was a realm far grander and more developed than many places Max had seen before.
Lucia stood beside him and spoke quietly.
"The Violet Star Palace controls all of this."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
The scale alone revealed why Violet Star Palace was considered one of the strongest third-rate forces in the Divine Realm.
Then he noticed something else.
Their star shuttle was not heading toward one of the ordinary planets.
It was flying toward the largest world in the entire realm.

That planet dominated the surrounding space like a celestial king among lesser stars. Its surface shimmered with oceans, continents, mountain chains, and giant cloud formations visible even from far away. Several moons circled it, while countless smaller transport vessels moved around its orbit like insects around a giant beast.
As the Black Dragon Clan shuttle approached the planetary vicinity, a ripple suddenly formed in the void ahead.
An old man appeared in front of the vessel as though space itself had opened to release him.

He wore violet robes embroidered with stars and carried no visible weapon. Yet the moment he appeared, every disciple inside felt immense pressure descend. His aura was calm and restrained, but even the slightest trace of it made many younger cultivators tense instinctively.
The shuttle slowed immediately.
Several elders of the Black Dragon Clan stepped forward respectfully.
The old man spoke in an indifferent voice.
"What force are you from?"
Mathew Grimes answered personally.
"We are the Black Dragon Clan of the Verdant Sky Realm, invited for the Smelting Trial."
The old man’s gaze swept across the vessel for a brief moment, as though examining every person inside at once.
Then he nodded.
"The identity is confirmed."
Without another wasted word, he turned and moved forward through the void.
"Follow me."
The star shuttle resumed movement and followed behind him.

As they passed through layers of planetary defenses, Max sensed countless formations surrounding the great world. Some concealed the atmosphere, some controlled entry routes, and others radiated killing intent powerful enough to erase intruders instantly.
Soon they entered the planet itself.
The moment they crossed the atmosphere, Max’s eyes sharpened.
The scale of the world was astonishing.

This planet was vastly larger than any he had seen so far in the Divine Realm. Its mountain ranges stretched like continents of stone. Rivers looked like silver seas from above. Forests were so immense that some regions appeared as green oceans. Giant cities covered lands larger than ordinary kingdoms, linked by roads of light and flying formations.
Even the energy here was denser and purer than most planets he had visited.
The old man continued leading them across the skies.
Below, Max saw territories, ancient towers, floating islands, giant arenas, and countless cultivators moving through the air as though such scenes were everyday life.
"This is only the outer regions," Lucia said softly.
Max looked at her.
"If this is the outer region, then the core of Violet Star Palace must be absurd."
Lucia smiled faintly.
"That is why they are one of the strongest 3rd rate forces."

The star shuttle continued forward under the guidance of the old man, crossing vast distances over landscapes so immense that even with their speed, minutes passed before one region fully ended and another began.

For the first time since arriving in the Divine Realm, Max truly felt the scale of a top third-rate force. It made him think if a top third rate force had such grandeur then what about the second rate forces and the firs rate forces.

The old man continued guiding them through the vast grounds of the Violet Star Palace’s outer region, his pace steady and unhurried. The deeper they traveled, the more astonished the disciples became.

Roads made from polished violet stone stretched in every direction, lined with glowing trees whose leaves shimmered faintly beneath the evening sky. Streams of spiritual water flowed beside the pathways, carrying a refreshing aura that calmed the mind the moment one drew near.
Soon, an enormous mansion-like palace rose before them.
It stood proudly atop a raised platform of white jade, its towering walls carved with stars, moons, and ancient furnace symbols that radiated age and dignity.

Rows of elegant pillars supported grand balconies, while lanterns of violet crystal hung from every corner, casting gentle light across the surroundings. The structure looked less like a temporary residence and more like the estate of a noble force.
Yet what shocked them even more was that this was not the only one.

As they drew closer, everyone noticed that similar mansion palaces were scattered across the entire region. Some stood beside lakes, others near gardens of spiritual herbs, while a few rested upon floating platforms connected by stone bridges.
At a glance, there were dozens of such residences, each grand enough to house an entire sect delegation.
Max narrowed his eyes as he observed the scene.

This was clearly a designated guest district of the Violet Star Palace, specially prepared for outside forces attending the Smelting Trial. The scale of it alone revealed how often large events were held here and how powerful the palace truly was. Even lodging for guests carried an aura of wealth that many lesser forces could never match.

chapters.title: Chapter 1618: Training!
paragraphs: The old man finally stopped in front of one of the mansions and turned toward them.
"You will stay here tonight."
His calm voice echoed lightly through the courtyard.
"The Smelting Trial will officially begin tomorrow morning. Use this time to recover yourselves and prepare. Once dawn arrives, representatives from every invited force will gather."
He swept his gaze across the disciples, his expression remaining indifferent.
"Do not wander recklessly. Certain areas of the Violet Star Palace are forbidden. Remain within the guest district unless summoned."
After speaking, the old man lightly waved his sleeve. The mansion gates slowly opened on their own, revealing a spacious inner courtyard, training grounds, and several luxurious chambers within.
"Rest well."
With those final words, the old man stepped away and soon vanished into the distance like drifting smoke.
For a moment, silence remained.
Then many disciples inhaled sharply as they stared at their temporary residence with shining eyes.
"This is where we stay for one night?"
"One night here is better than a year in some dormitories."
"The Violet Star Palace truly deserves its reputation."
Even Lucia’s usually calm eyes flickered with surprise, while Isabella quietly admired the beauty of the courtyard.
Once inside the mansion, the disciples of the Black Dragon Clan were immediately shown the scale of Violet Star Palace’s hospitality.

The interior was vast and elegant, with halls lined by smooth crystal walls that reflected streams of soft violet light. Every room carried a rich concentration of spiritual energy, making even breathing feel refreshing. Spacious guest chambers had already been prepared, each furnished with cultivation mats, medicinal incense burners, and polished furniture crafted from rare spirit wood.
The younger disciples quickly dispersed.

Some entered secluded rooms to meditate and stabilize their cultivation in preparation for tomorrow. Others took out weapons and began polishing them with serious expressions. A few gathered in small groups, discussing rumors about the Smelting Trial and the geniuses who would participate from other forces. Nervousness and anticipation could be felt everywhere.
No one wished to embarrass the Black Dragon Clan tomorrow.
Max had only just entered the courtyard when a familiar voice sounded behind him.
"Max. Lucia. Isabella. Follow me."
Lady Virelia stood there with her arms crossed, her long hair swaying gently as she looked at the three of them with sharp eyes. There was no trace of leisure on her face.
The three exchanged glances before immediately following.

She led them deeper into the mansion grounds until they arrived at a private training field located behind the residence. The area was surrounded by high formation walls, while the ground itself was forged from dark star metal capable of enduring heavy impacts. Ancient runes glowed faintly beneath the surface.
Lady Virelia turned around and spoke calmly.
"You three will train a little before resting."
Lucia smiled faintly, already understanding what was coming.
Isabella blinked once, then looked toward Max with interest.
Lady Virelia pointed at the center of the field.
"A three-way battle. Lucia and Isabella against Max."
Max almost thought he heard wrong.
"Against both of them?"
Lady Virelia’s lips curved slightly.

"You heard correctly. If I am not wrong you will be targeted heavily tomorrow and so you might as well be prepared for this. But don’t use any techniques in this battle. Just use your basic attacks to fight. "
Max exhaled slowly before stepping onto the field.

He knew very well that among the three, he was currently the weakest in direct cultivation. Lucia possessed deep and steady strength with frightening combat control, while Isabella’s Imperial Bloodline gave her a natural superiority that even elders respected.
Yet Max’s eyes did not waver.
The moment Lady Virelia waved her hand, the battle began.
Lucia moved first.

Her figure blurred like a phantom as she closed the distance instantly, her palm carrying compressed force of black flames strong enough to crack mountains. At the same time, Isabella raised one hand and released streams of black dragon flames that curved through the air like living serpents, sealing Max’s retreat paths.
A normal disciple would have been defeated in the opening breath.
But Max stepped forward instead of back.

Lightning exploded beneath his feet as he twisted through the narrow gap between the flames, then tilted his body just enough to avoid Lucia’s palm by a hair’s breadth. The force of her strike blasted the ground behind him apart.
Without hesitation, Max countered with a fist toward Lucia’s ribs.
Lucia blocked, but her eyes flickered slightly at the force hidden in the strike.

Before either could continue, Isabella descended from above with black fire condensed around her leg. Max raised both arms and received the blow head-on. The impact drove him several meters backward, his boots carving deep lines across the star metal floor.
Lady Virelia watched silently.
The battle only intensified.

Lucia attacked with relentless close-range precision. Isabella dominated the field with wide destructive pressure. Their teamwork was not intentional, yet both naturally cornered Max from two directions.
Still, Max refused to collapse.

He moved constantly, reading their attacks through his Dimensional Sovereign Body. He used speed to break angles, timing to create openings, and ruthless counters whenever either underestimated him. Several times he was struck and sent reeling, yet every time he rose instantly and charged back in.
At one point, Lucia’s palm locked onto his chest while Isabella’s flame spear descended from behind.
Even Lady Virelia narrowed her eyes.

Yet Max suddenly spun low, using Lucia’s incoming force to redirect himself sideways. Her palm missed by inches while Isabella’s spear passed through the space Max had occupied. Max then drove an elbow into Lucia’s shoulder and kicked Isabella backward before leaping away.
Lucia laughed softly.
"You are such a tough guy to fight."
Isabella’s usually calm eyes shone brighter.
"He is troublesome."
Minutes turned into an hour.
Sweat covered the three geniuses. Cracks spread across the training field. Shockwaves repeatedly slammed into the barrier walls.
Yet one fact remained clear.
Though Max was the weakest in realm and raw power, he had not been defeated.
He stood there breathing heavily, bruised and battered, but still upright. His eyes burned hotter than before.
Lady Virelia finally raised a hand, ending the match.
The field fell silent.
She looked at Max for a long moment before speaking.
"Good."
That single word from her carried more praise than a hundred compliments.
Then she turned toward all three.
"This is enough for now. Go ahead and rest you three."
Max wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth and smiled faintly before heading to his respective room to rest.
Only Lady Virelia remained standing on the training ground.
